title: SALTEK
category: Renewable Energy · IoT · Artificial Intelligence · Smart Agriculture · Sustainable Farming
description: SALTEK is an intelligent solar-powered irrigation system designed to protect smallholder farm soil from salt damage across North Africa and Africa. The system autonomously blends water from two sources using real-time TDS salinity sensing and a weighted mixing algorithm to deliver every irrigation cycle at the precise EC level safe for the crop and soil. A built-in GSM module sends plain language SMS alerts directly to the farmer's basic mobile phone, while an LLM API translates all technical sensor data into simple human-readable messages — no smartphone, no app, and no technical knowledge required.
problem: Across North Africa, 84% of groundwater exceeds safe salinity limits and 35% of agricultural soils are already salt-damaged. Farmers understand the risk but have no affordable tool to act on it. Existing industrial salinity management solutions cost thousands of dollars and require technical expertise completely out of reach for smallholder farmers — who represent the majority of Africa's agricultural workforce and have no choice but to keep irrigating with water that is slowly destroying their land.
solution: SALTEK proposes an autonomous low-cost irrigation system that combines:
solutionPoints: Real-time TDS salinity sensing across three water points
Weighted mixing algorithm to blend two water sources at the correct EC ratio
Four-pump autonomous control via ESP32 and relay modules
HC-SR04 ultrasonic tank level monitoring and water level detection
DS1302 real-time clock for daily irrigation scheduling
MQTT-based wireless communication between two ESP32 microcontrollers
Arduino Uno managing autonomous solar and battery power switching
GSM module sending real-time SMS alerts for tank status, irrigation events, and system warnings
LLM API integration translating sensor data into plain language farmer notifications
impact: IEEE IAS IPCSD Student Design Competition 2026 Submission. SALTEK directly addresses one of Africa's most urgent agricultural crises — soil salinization affecting over 200 million hectares across the continent. By intelligently blending saline and clean water sources, the system reduces salt accumulation in soil with every irrigation cycle, creating a compounding improvement in soil health over time. Farmers spend less on purchased clean water, preserve the long-term productivity of their land, and receive automated guidance through a basic mobile phone — no technical knowledge required. Built for under $100 and powered entirely by solar energy, SALTEK makes precision irrigation accessible to the smallholder farmers who need it most, protecting their livelihoods and the agricultural future of the African continent.

title: SafeBehaviour
description: SafeBehaviour is an intelligent industrial safety platform designed to improve worker safety, cybersecurity awareness, and energy efficiency through smart behavioural monitoring. The system uses wearable smart badges, edge gateways, AI analytics, digital twin simulation, and an admin dashboard to detect risky behaviours and support real-time decision-making in industrial environments.
problem: Industrial environments face several risks related to unsafe worker behaviour, equipment interaction, cybersecurity threats, and energy misuse. Traditional monitoring systems often lack real-time behavioural intelligence and do not provide a unified view of safety, cyber, and energy-related risks.
solution: The project introduces a human-centered industrial intelligence system combining:
solutionPoints: Smart Badge for motion, proximity, temperature, and identity sensing
Edge Gateway for secure telemetry collection and cloud transmission
Behavioural Risk Index for safety, cyber, and energy risk scoring
Machine learning models for alert prediction and anomaly detection
Dashboard for supervisors to monitor KPIs, alerts, and worker behaviour
Digital Twin and Agentic AI for simulation, reasoning, and decision support
Secure badge architecture with authentication, firmware protection, and tamper detection
impact: SafeBehaviour supports safer and smarter industrial operations by enabling real-time risk detection, faster supervisor intervention, behavioural history tracking, and improved compliance monitoring. The project reflects IEEE IAS ENIS SBC’s vision of using AI, IoT, and human-centered engineering to build safer, more secure, and more energy-efficient industrial environments.

title: AI-Optimized School-Clinic Microgrids
category: Renewable Energy - Artificial Intelligence - Smart Microgrids - Healthcare - Education
description: AI-Optimized School-Clinic Microgrids is a sustainable energy project designed to support rural African communities by connecting schools and nearby clinics through intelligent solar microgrids. The project uses LSTM neural networks to forecast energy demand, optimize power distribution, and prioritize critical healthcare loads such as vaccine refrigerators.
problem: Many rural communities in Africa suffer from unreliable electricity, affecting both education and healthcare. Schools lack stable power for classrooms and computer labs, while clinics face vaccine storage failures due to refrigeration interruptions.
solution: The project proposes an AI-enhanced microgrid system that combines:
solutionPoints: Solar panels and LiFePO4 battery storage
Raspberry Pi-based edge computing
LSTM models for energy forecasting
IoT-enabled smart relays for priority load control
Automatic switching to protect vaccine refrigeration
Mobile payment integration to support maintenance and sustainability
impact: Third Place Student Award — IEEE Smart Village Student Paper Competition 2025. The system achieved strong results, including 100% vaccine viability, 98.2% system uptime, improved school operating hours, reduced clinic energy costs, and monthly revenue generation from energy sharing. This project demonstrates how smart energy systems can improve healthcare, education, and community resilience in underserved regions.

title: Zaytouna Sense
category: Smart Agriculture · IoT · AI · Mobile Application · Sustainable Farming
description: Zaytouna Sense is an AI and IoT-based smart agriculture project designed to support Tunisian olive farmers. The system helps farmers monitor their farms in real time, optimize irrigation, detect olive tree diseases through image analysis, and receive alerts through a mobile application or WhatsApp.
problem: Olive farmers in Tunisia face several challenges, including water scarcity, crop diseases, pest attacks, and limited access to real-time farm data. Traditional monitoring methods can delay intervention and lead to water waste or yield losses.
solution: The project introduces a smart farming platform combining:
solutionPoints: IoT sensors for soil moisture, humidity, and temperature monitoring
ESP32-based control of irrigation pumps and valves
AI models for irrigation recommendations
Disease detection using uploaded olive leaf images
Mobile application built with Flutter
Flask backend with MongoDB database
WhatsApp and in-app notifications
Community dashboard for farmers to share alerts and experiences
impact: Winner — IASTAM Tech Challenge. Zaytouna Sense promotes smarter and more sustainable olive farming by helping farmers make faster decisions, reduce water waste, prevent crop losses, and improve productivity. The project reflects IEEE IAS ENIS SBC’s commitment to using engineering and digital innovation to solve real agricultural challenges in Tunisia.

title: Blockchain-Secured Industrial IoT Network
category: Industrial IoT · Blockchain · AI · Cybersecurity · Industry 4.0
description: Blockchain-Secured Industrial IoT Network is a cybersecurity project designed to secure industrial IoT environments through decentralized device authentication, real-time anomaly detection, and equipment traceability. The system combines Blockchain, AI, IoT, and cloud technologies to protect smart factories and industrial automation systems from unauthorized access and cyber threats.
problem: Industrial IoT networks are increasingly exposed to cybersecurity risks such as unauthorized device access, data breaches, equipment fraud, and abnormal network behavior. Traditional centralized security systems can create single points of failure and may not be sufficient for modern Industry 4.0 environments.
solution: The project proposes a secure IIoT framework combining:
solutionPoints: ESP32 and PLC devices communicating through MQTT
Blockchain-based authentication using Hyperledger Fabric or Ethereum
Smart contracts for device registration and ownership validation
RFID tracking for industrial equipment traceability
LSTM-based AI model for real-time anomaly detection
Flask and React.js web dashboard for monitoring alerts and device status
AWS Lambda and AWS S3 for cloud execution and secure data storage
impact: IEEE IAS CMD Myron Zucker Undergraduate Student Design Contest Submission. The system achieved strong performance results, including 95% anomaly detection accuracy, 80% reduction in unauthorized access, 1.5-second authentication latency, and 1.2-second device onboarding speed. This project demonstrates how blockchain and AI can strengthen industrial cybersecurity, improve traceability, and support safer, smarter industrial automation systems.

title: Smart & Sustainable Olive-Centric Industrial Zones
category: Smart Agriculture · IoT · AI · Blockchain · Renewable Energy
description: Smart and Sustainable Olive-Centric Industrial Zones is a project developed by IEEE IAS ENIS SBC to modernize Tunisia’s olive sector using IoT, Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and renewable energy. The project proposes smart industrial zones dedicated to olive agriculture, aiming to improve irrigation, energy efficiency, logistics, traceability, and waste management.
problem: Tunisia’s olive sector faces major challenges such as water scarcity, energy inefficiency, poor waste management, outdated infrastructure, and lack of supply chain transparency.
solution: The project introduces a smart ecosystem combining:
solutionPoints: IoT sensors for real-time crop and soil monitoring
AI-based irrigation recommendations
Blockchain for olive oil traceability and certification
Solar-powered irrigation and battery storage
Smart logistics with cold storage and autonomous transport
Waste-to-product systems converting olive waste into biogas and biomass
impact: 1st Place — IAS Technical Challenge, TSYP12. The project supports a more sustainable olive industry by reducing water and energy waste, improving production transparency, creating new value from agricultural waste, and promoting smart agriculture in Tunisia.
